title: Improve the lower bound for R(4,6) with a 36-vertex graph
statement: Does there exist a finite simple undirected graph on exactly 36 vertices having neither a clique of four vertices nor an independent set of six vertices? A witness proves R(4,6) >= 37; ruling out all such graphs would prove R(4,6)=36.
source_locator: DS1 revision 18, Table Ia for the lower bound and Table Ib for the improved upper bound; Exoo's R(4,6) collection.
status_basis: The 2026 survey gives 36 <= R(4,6) <= 40, with the upper bound in Table Ib rather than the older Table Ia entry. The author collection supplies 35-vertex witnesses. No authoritative later resolution was located in a scoped check on 2026-10-14.

epistemic_layers.formal_validity: Only a checked finite witness or a proof covering the declared space establishes the mathematical claim.
epistemic_layers.empirical_support: No physical model, empirical data or experiment is needed.

difficulty.basis: The unrestricted target is a research frontier; a bounded trial has no assured outcome.

correctness.basis: No project candidate solution has been submitted or independently reviewed.

novelty.basis: Future results must be checked against live sources and existing computational records.

significance.basis: A verified improvement would resolve a finite case or tighten a recognized extremal bound.

plain_summary: Find a graph on 36 vertices in which neither four vertices are all joined nor six vertices are all mutually unjoined. Its complete correctness check involves fewer than two million small subsets.
assumptions: The graph is simple, undirected and has exactly 36 vertices.
A K_4 means all six edges among four vertices are present; an independent six-set means all fifteen edges among six vertices are absent.
An optional edit neighborhood is not assumed to contain every possible solution.
scope: A one-vertex improvement of the constructive bound for R(4,6). The proposed first milestone uses public 35-vertex graphs as seeds; the novelty of that restricted search is not established.
target: Construct a 36-vertex (4,6)-graph. Curator-proposed milestone: use Exoo's 37 listed 35-vertex graphs, add one freely adjacent vertex, and allow at most four changes to edges among the original vertices.
success_criteria: Supply a complete 36-vertex adjacency record with no K_4 and no independent six-set, checked by an independent program.
Identify and validate the 37 seeds; define the edit budget on unordered pairs among the original 35 vertices.
Cap the proposed search at 8 CPU-hours and 16 GiB RAM. These are resource limits for an experiment, not an estimate of the cost of resolving the problem.
Preserve checked witnesses and restricted UNSAT certificates. A timeout or a failed neighborhood search does not imply R(4,6)=36.
known_results: The 2026 survey gives 36 <= R(4,6) <= 40; its stronger upper bound appears in Table Ib.
Exoo's collection contains 37 constructions at order 35, rather than an exhaustive classification of all such graphs.
The survey excludes an improved lower bound from circulant graphs at this order, so a cyclic-only restriction is unsuitable.
significance: A valid 36-vertex graph improves a longstanding lower bound by one. A full nonexistence proof would determine the number exactly, but is far beyond the proposed local search.

requirements.data: The 37 attributed graph files linked by SRC-MATH-203. Their source and content identifiers should accompany any extension result.
requirements.compute: Proposed cap: 8 CPU-hours and 16 GiB RAM for all seeds together. The witness has 630 possible edges; independent brute-force verification examines C(36,4)=58,905 four-sets and C(36,6)=1,947,792 six-sets. Search and global nonexistence can be far more expensive.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Ordinary finite graph theory. The seed list and four-edge radius define a curator-proposed restricted experiment only.

ai_assessment.rationale: The proposed bounded construction trial has reusable attributed seeds and a transparent independent checker. The recommendation concerns reviewability and controlled scope, not an expectation of solving the full problem.

clarity.reason: Fixed vertex count and two forbidden subsets are explicit.

decomposability.reason: Seed validation, extension generation and witness verification are independent components.

methods.reason: Published constructions and a maintained survey support concrete graph-search approaches.

search_or_symbolic.reason: The problem has a direct Boolean encoding and exact local predicates.

checkability.reason: Every forbidden four-set and six-set can be checked by a separate small program.

expertise.reason: Implementing the checker is elementary; useful search design needs combinatorial experience.

significance.reason: A witness advances a recognized small Ramsey bound.

verification_difficulty.reason: A positive graph has a transparent exhaustive checker; this rating does not apply to a global impossibility claim.

ai_assessment.uncertainty: No model or seed neighborhood has been tested. Existing expert searches may already have covered these neighborhoods, and success within the proposed cap is unknown.
ai_assessment.model_scope: No named model evaluated; assumes tool-using AI with exact graph algorithms, SAT encodings and reproducible solver inputs.

methods: One-vertex seed extension with bounded edge changes
SAT or local search with forbidden-subgraph penalties
Checked certificates for explicitly restricted neighborhoods
obstacles: The known seed collection is small and not exhaustive.
Search may rediscover an already checked neighborhood.
The complementary color convention can be accidentally reversed.
A wrong proof of symmetry breaking can invalidate a negative result.

steps: Independently parse and validate the 36-vertex simple graph.
Enumerate all four-subsets and reject complete ones.
Enumerate all six-subsets and reject independent ones.
Confirm the lower-bound implication is R(4,6) >= 37, not >= 36.
For a negative neighborhood result, check the encoding, seeds, edit radius and certificate separately.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Low for a positive witness; high for an unrestricted impossibility proof. Restricted failures need precise scope and provenance.
validation.statement_alignment: A 36-vertex witness improves the Ramsey lower bound to 37. Only ruling out every 36-vertex graph would prove the exact value 36.

known_attempts: Exoo publishes 37 order-35 constructions; the 2026 survey cites improved upper-bound computations. These records motivate a finite construction task without implying AI performance.
unresolved_checks: Fetch and independently validate the individual seed files before a trial.
Check whether four-edge extension neighborhoods have already been exhausted.
Confirm the live survey bounds before describing a result as an improvement.

attribution.citation: Exoo (2012), R(4,6) Colorings, 37 constructions of K_35; Radziszowski (2026), Small Ramsey Numbers, revision 18, Tables Ia and Ib, which credits the upper-bound computations to Angeltveit and McKay.
attribution.curator_credit: Compiled for Theory Research Atlas with AI assistance.

status_search.result: The 2026 survey retains the interval 36 to 40; the author's collection provides order-35 seeds. A scoped October search found no authoritative later improvement or resolution.
status_search.limitations: Individual seed files and the cited upper-bound computation have not been rerun. Unpublished searches may cover the proposed milestone.
